title: Plate Tectonics
seo_title: Grade 7 Plate Tectonics Worksheets: Continental Drift, Seafloor Spreading and Plate Boundaries
standard_text: Analyze and interpret data on the distribution of fossils and rocks, continental shapes, and seafloor structures to provide evidence of the past plate motions.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on plate tectonics (NGSS MS-ESS2-3): evidence from fossils, rocks, continent shapes and the seafloor, seafloor age data, and plate boundaries. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Fossils, rocks and the seafloor show that plates move.
key_sub: Matching coastlines, fossils and rocks, plus seafloor that ages away from ridges, show continents have moved over millions of years.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth's outer layer is broken into tectonic plates that move a few centimeters per year. Scientists use four kinds of evidence:

  • Continental shapes: South America and Africa fit like puzzle pieces.
  • Fossils: the same land plants and animals (Glossopteris, Mesosaurus) are found on continents now separated by oceans.
  • Rock formations: matching rock layers and mountain belts on different continents.
  • Seafloor structures: mid-ocean ridges, deep trenches, and seafloor that gets older farther from the ridges.

At divergent boundaries plates move apart, at convergent boundaries they push together, and at transform boundaries they slide past each other.

Example

The same fossil fern is found in Africa and India. What does this suggest?

Plants could not cross the ocean.

Answer: The continents were once joined.

Example

Where is the youngest seafloor?

New rock forms where plates spread apart.

Answer: at mid-ocean ridges

Common mistakes

  • Thinking continents float on the ocean.
  • Thinking plates move meters per year. They move centimeters.
  • Thinking the oldest seafloor is at the ridge.

faq.q: What evidence shows that continents have moved?
faq.a: Matching continent shapes, the same fossils and rock layers on different continents, and seafloor features like mid-ocean ridges and seafloor ages.

faq.q: How fast do tectonic plates move?
faq.a: About 2 to 10 centimeters per year, roughly as fast as fingernails grow.

faq.q: What are the three kinds of plate boundaries?
faq.a: Divergent (moving apart), convergent (pushing together) and transform (sliding past each other).

items.q: Who first proposed continental drift using fossils and continent shapes?
items.e: He proposed it in 1912.

items.q: Do continents float on the ocean?
c: No. Continents are part of plates that move over the hot, slowly flowing mantle.
items.e: The mantle rock can flow very slowly.

items.q: About how fast do plates move?
c: a few centimeters per year, about as fast as fingernails grow
items.e: Slow, but it adds up over millions of years.

items.q: What forms at a mid-ocean ridge?
c: new ocean floor from rising magma
items.e: This is seafloor spreading.

items.q: Mia reads: “The same kinds of rock layers and mountain belts appear in eastern North America and western Europe.” What kind of evidence for plate motion is this?
items.e: All four kinds of evidence show that the continents and seafloor have moved.

items.e: All four kinds of evidence show that the continents and seafloor have moved.

items.q: Why couldn't Mesosaurus have swum across the Atlantic?
c: It was a small freshwater reptile that could not cross a salty ocean.
items.e: Its fossils support the idea that the continents were joined.
